label: rem:burau-invariant-form-prior-art
title: Prior art: the Burau representation preserves a sesquilinear form
html:
For a matrix M over \mathbb{Z}[t, t^{-1}] let M^* be its transpose with every entry p(t) replaced by p(t^{-1}). Squier proves that there is a nonsingular (n-1) \times (n-1) matrix J_0 over \mathbb{Z}[t, t^{-1}] with \beta(w)^* J_0\, \beta(w) = J_0 for every w \in B_n, where \beta is the reduced Burau representation [squier1984, Theorem, p. 199]. Over \mathbb{Z}[s, s^{-1}] with s^2 = t, rescaling the basis by s^a turns J_0 into the Hermitian matrix

J = (s + s^{-1})\, I - \sum_a \left(e_{a-1,a} + e_{a,a+1}\right),

and each generator then acts as the reflection \beta_i(v) = v - (s^2 + 1)\, \langle e_i, v \rangle / \langle e_i, e_i \rangle \; e_i, with \langle v, w \rangle = v^* J w [squier1984, \S 3, eqs. (6)--(7), p. 201].

The proof of the Borromean fibre theorem uses the Burau representation at t = -1. There the substitution t \mapsto t^{-1} fixes t, so Squier's identity specialises to \beta(w)^{\mathsf{T}} J_0(-1)\, \beta(w) = J_0(-1): an integral bilinear form preserved by the image of B_3. The proof does not use this form; it argues from traces and the R, L normal form in \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z}).

Two points stop the form from being used at t = -1 without further work. Nonsingularity is a statement over \mathbb{Z}[t, t^{-1}], so whether J_0(-1) is still nonsingular, and what its signature is, has not been checked here. And at s = i the diagonal entry \langle e_i, e_i \rangle = s + s^{-1} is zero, so the reflection formula above is not defined at that point. The corpus's other t = -1 object, the Jordan block of the Hecke generator at q = i, is a different module, and Squier's form says nothing about it directly.
